observations: Desktop fish silhouettes and staggered spacing read clearly; reef plants and open sand routes remain visible.
Phone HUD and real touch controls fit with no horizontal overflow; central play view is tighter and the action prompt overlaps the lower squid.
Current-only native GL views show the actual scene without DOM overlays; camera projection and static resource identities passed the capture gates.
limits: Static images do not establish motion smoothness; live simulation and shader gates are separate.
Behavioral fixtures arrange encounters for regression checks; natural visual captures do not.

independent.method: Inspected all eight saved PNGs using view_image. Read compact capture manifest for source, native input and submission context. No browser or GPU work, production edits, actor repositioning or new captures.
independent.decision: Accept this enhancement pass with the visual limits below.

views.assessment: The red mantle and broad fins have a clear silhouette and volume against the pale sand. The distant fish cluster reads as a small living school rather than a rigid row. Kelp and seagrass frame an open route, with rock and coral clusters leaving room around the player. HUD panels and controls fit; the central player is unobstructed.

Nearby fish are individually distinguishable, with staggered depth, varied headings, forked tails and readable fins. Their visible spread is organic. The pale target ring and fleeing readout agree with the manifest. The large squid remains distinct from the fish and reef. Plants retain recognizable individual leaves and clustered basal areas; no obvious shader tearing or detached leaf pieces appear.

The low-quality GL view still has clear sand, reef, water depth and a readable squid. The DOM screenshot shows all controls within the 390 by 844 viewport, with legible labels and no visible horizontal overflow. The upper mantle and nearby target fish remain visible. The narrower camera crops most of the fleeing school; this is consistent with the manifest's two fish in the frustum.

The sand-colored octopus has a smooth mantle, fine speckling, distinct tapered arms and a useful contact shadow. Foreground sand provides a clear travel area; coral, rock and kelp clusters give the reef depth without blocking the player. Grass appears attached to its basal patches. Desktop status and controls are readable and do not cover the animal. No fish are visible here, as the natural schools remain outside this camera's frustum.

limits: These are current-only static captures. They establish appearance and layout, not before/after visual superiority, motion smoothness, plant-flow coherence, gameplay usability over time or hardware performance.

The phone's status panels and touch controls use much of the canvas. Its action prompt crosses the lower squid body and controls approach the fin tips. The upper mantle remains visible and controls fit, but preserving more of the central scene during a close chase is a useful future UI refinement.

Thin bright contact fringes are visible around several rocks in the sand. There is no matched baseline evidence here to attribute them to this pass; contact shading is a possible future visual polish target.
Root pinning, shader normals and nonrigid flow require the independent numeric/native tests; static images alone cannot prove those properties.
